topic.name: Solving Polynomial Equations Using the GCF

question.explanation:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form $P_n(p)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} 4p^2+21p&=3p^2+2p^3\\[3pt] -2p^3+4p^2+21p&=3p^2\\[3pt] -2p^3+p^2+21p&=0 \end{align}

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $-p.$ We can factor out the $-p$ as follows: \begin{align} -2p^3+p^2+21p&=0\\[3pt] -p(2p^2 - p - 21) & = 0\\[3pt] \end{align}

Now, we factor the expression $2p^2 - p - 21$ as follows: \begin{align} -p(2p^2 - p - 21)&=0\\[3pt] -p(2p -7)(p + 3) & = 0 \end{align}

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $p = 0,$ $p = \dfrac{7}{2},$ and $p = -3.$

example.title: Solving a Cubic Equation by Rearranging

question.explanation:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form $P_n(x)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} 10x^3 + 2x^2 &= \dfrac{9}{2}x -10x^2\\[3pt] 10x^3 + 12x^2 &= \dfrac{9}{2}x\\[3pt] 10x^3 + 12x^2 -\dfrac{9}{2}x& = 0 \end{align}

Next, we can factor out the $\dfrac{x}{2}$ as follows: \begin{align} 10x^3 + 12x^2 -\dfrac{9}{2}x & = 0\\[3pt] \dfrac{x}{2}\left(20x^2 + 24x -9\right) & = 0\\[3pt] \end{align}

Now, we factor the expression $20x^2 + 24x -9$ as follows: \begin{align} \dfrac{x}{2}\left(20x^2 + 24x -9\right) & = 0\\[3pt] \dfrac{x}{2}(10x -3 )(2x +3) & = 0 \end{align}

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $x = 0,$ $x = \dfrac{3}{10},$ and $x = -\dfrac{3}{2}.$

example.title: Solving a Cubic Equation by Rearranging

question.explanation:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(y) = 0,$ that is \[ 8y^4 + 4y^3 - 12y^2 = 0. \]

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $4y^2.$ We can factor out the $4y^2$ as follows: \begin{align} %8y^4 + 4y^3 - 12y^2 & = 0 \\[3pt] 4y^2(2y^2 + y - 3) & = 0 \end{align}

Now, we factor the expression $2y^2 + y - 3$ as follows: \begin{align} 4y^2(2y^2 + y - 3) & = 0\\[3pt] 4y^2(2y + 3)(y - 1) & = 0 \end{align}

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $y = 0,$ $y = -\dfrac{3}{2},$ and $y = 1.$

example.title: Solving a Higher-Order Polynomial Equation With No Constant Term

question.text: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(q) = 24 q^5 - 62 q^4 + 14 q^3.$
question.explanation:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(q) = 0,$ that is \[ 24 q^5 - 62 q^4 + 14 q^3 = 0. \]

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $2q^3.$ We can factor out the $2q^3$ as follows: \begin{align} %24 q^5 - 62 q^4 + 14 q^3 & = 0 \\[3pt] 2q^3(12q^2-31q +7) & = 0 \end{align}

Now, we factor the expression $12q^2-31q +7$ as follows: \begin{align} 2q^3(12q^2-31q +7) & = 0\\[3pt] 2q^3(4q - 1)(3q -7) & = 0 \end{align}

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $q = 0,$ $q = \dfrac{1}{4},$ and $q = \dfrac{7}{3}.$
